clue.text: Iron starts to go on the blink, then radio

indicators.note: a device on the blink is malfunctioning, so the letters before it come out jumbled

parts.note: the two words supply all ten letters

explanation.surface: An iron begins to malfunction, and then so does the radio: a bad day for household appliances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like a separate appliance, but its letters join 'starts' as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A transistor is an old informal name for a small portable radio, after the component inside it.

clue.text: Leave, going uphill in carriage

indicators.note: in a down entry, going uphill means reading from the bottom upward, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to part is to leave or go away

explanation.surface: Someone sets off up a hill riding in a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Punishment given by a belt set about bumpkin?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: set about here means placed around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to belt along is to tear, to rush
a hick is a country bumpkin

explanation.surface: A yokel is attacked and given a beating with a belt as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt' reads as a strap for whipping, or a blow; here it means to rush along, i.e. tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone a thick ear is a British idiom for hitting them round the head as a punishment.

clue.text: Mates worry unduly about the song

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the next word
unduly suggests something done improperly, so the letters are put into the wrong order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Friends fret excessively over a particular song.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy Weather is a famous 1933 jazz standard, sung by Ethel Waters and Lena Horne among others.

clue.text: They fleece judge on board ship

indicators.note: something on board a vessel is inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
one who hears a case, i.e. judges it

explanation.surface: Swindlers rip off a magistrate travelling on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' suggests cheating; here it is literal, taking the wool off sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearers are workers who clip the wool, the fleece, from sheep.

clue.text: Excursion abroad in front of galley

parts.note: out, as in out of the country or away
taken as written

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of galley

explanation.surface: A trip overseas, sitting at the front of an oared ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short trip or excursion for pleasure.

clue.text: Iceberg in local fjord

indicators.note: in points to letters sitting inside the words that follow, running across the break

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An iceberg floats in a nearby Norwegian inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A calf is a mass of ice that has broken off a glacier or larger iceberg.

clue.text: A gypsy with a distinctive smell

parts.note: taken as written
the Roma are the Romani people, traditionally called gypsies

explanation.surface: A traveller carrying a particular odour.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a characteristic smell, usually pleasant.

clue.text: Rodent filmed out by river

indicators.note: out here means disordered or wrong, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A rodent is caught on camera outdoors beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The field mouse is a small wild rodent of woods and farmland.

clue.text: Refurbished an hotel in a town on the Shannon

indicators.note: refurbishing means renovating and rearranging, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A renovated hotel in an Irish riverside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Athlone is a town in the Irish midlands that straddles the River Shannon.

clue.text: This may be used by a recovery vehicle in poor wet ground

definitions.text: This may be used by a recovery vehicle

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters before it are broken up and re-formed

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A breakdown truck might need this to pull a car out of soggy terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as soil, fitting the muddy scene, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A towrope is the line a breakdown truck attaches to haul a stranded car.

clue.text: The new stadium built for a London football club

indicators.note: something built is put together from parts, so the letters are assembled into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A new ground is constructed for a London club.
explanation.walkthrough: Apt: West Ham did move into a new stadium, the former Olympic Stadium, in 2016.
explanation.definitionFit: West Ham United is a Premier League football club in east London.

clue.text: PM is to touch down in a place in the Arctic Ocean

definitions.text: a place in the Arctic Ocean

parts.note: David Cameron, UK Prime Minister 2010 to 2016
taken as written
an aircraft lands when it touches down

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's plane is due to land somewhere in the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameron Island is an uninhabited island in Canada's Arctic archipelago.

clue.text: Restoring development around West Berlin, perhaps

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the reshaped letters enclose the next piece
a development is a change of form, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: Rebuilding work encircles the western part of the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Berlin is not the city but Irving Berlin, who wrote White Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin is an example of a composer of popular songs, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Casseroles, say, old and new, Vera smashed

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: smashed means broken to pieces, so the preceding letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Vera has broken her cooking pots, the old ones and the new.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovenware is heat-proof dishes for the oven, and casseroles are one example.

clue.text: Mad with nag at Kelso's last

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
a hack is a broken-down horse, a nag

indicators.note: a word's last is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of Kelso

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a poor horse at Kelso racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Kelso is a Scottish Borders town with a racecourse. 'Mad' means crazy here; whacko is usually spelt wacko.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacko is an informal word for crazy or eccentric, a synonym of mad.

clue.text: Girl causing unexpected stir in Communist country

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the following word

parts.note: China is a Communist state

indicators.note: unexpected suggests things are not in their usual order, so the word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A girl provokes an unforeseen commotion in a Communist state.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina is a female first name, and crosswords use 'girl' for any such name.

clue.text: Room overlooking yard in a French skiing centre

parts.note: a chamber is a room
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A room looking out onto a courtyard at a French ski resort.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'overlooking' means the first piece stands above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambéry is a city in the French Alps, a base for nearby ski resorts.

clue.text: Good chap, engaging alternative comedian

indicators.note: engaging means taking in or holding, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a chap is a man
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A decent fellow books an alternative stand-up act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative comedian' looks like one phrase, but 'alternative' gives OR and 'comedian' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Dave Gorman is an English comedian known for documentary-style stand-up shows.

clue.text: Rings about artist having wild dreams

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the next

parts.note: a bell chimes when it rings
RA, Royal Academician, is crossword shorthand for an artist

explanation.surface: A painter woken by bells has vivid dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a fanciful illusion or impossible fantasy, so chimeras are wild imaginings.

clue.text: Outstanding gesture

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a movement made to convey a message

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for a fine gesture, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means remarkable; as a noun it means a sign made to communicate.

clue.text: More than one good bloke lacking social graces appears in sharp suit

definitions.text: More than one good bloke lacking social graces

parts.note: rough as in harsh or sharp in manner
diamonds is one of the four suits of playing cards

explanation.surface: A decent but uncouth man turns up in a smart suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharp suit' looks like stylish tailoring; the suit is from a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough diamond is an idiom for someone kind-hearted but unpolished in manners.

clue.text: Disrupt cheerful group

parts.note: feeling up is feeling cheerful
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Breaking up a happy gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset plans or arrangements is to disrupt them.

clue.text: So fortunate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an interjection opening a remark, as in 'So, what now?'

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'very lucky', but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word serves as a conversational opener and as an adjective for something lucky or advisable.

clue.text: International to manage trial

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A national player's job is to handle a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A test run is a trial operation to check something works.

clue.text: Weave intricate net before getting to port?

indicators.note: intricate means tangled and complicated, so the next word's letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A boat crew mends a complicated net on the way into harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests a harbour, backed by the net and the question mark; it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist or weave strands together.

clue.text: Harshly rebuke class

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old verb for scolding angrily
second meaning: a grade or category

explanation.surface: A teacher tells off a whole form.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to scold severely; the noun means a grade or rank, as in second-rate.

clue.text: What the footballer did is co-operated

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally kicked a ball around in a game
second meaning: the idiom for going along with others

explanation.surface: A footballer's activity amounts to working with others.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom meaning to co-operate or go along with a plan.
